output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. The past 26 weeks average 0.354% with an upper normal edge of 0.482%, and 0.411% is inside that band. Three earlier weeks were higher and were investigated with no fault found. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard counts match raw logs, so it isn't a counting artefact. Bookings and support complaints did not change. The "new pods error at twice the rate" finding is a warm-up effect. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image, shows the same gap, caused by cold caches and read-replica timeouts. It adds only 10–20 errors, so it says nothing about v4.18. I can't rule out v4.18, the replica move or partner-sync traffic as small contributors. Nothing shows any of them mattered. Recommendation: don't roll back and don't mute alerting, since muting would remove a protective control. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to next week. Escalate to an incident only if next week exceeds the band or the page fires. That is where I'd then look at the replica move and the fetchwell bump.
